label: early input positions (t=1-4) after m/t/p/i/o/1 tokens
explanation: Most activation mass (79%) is in the original-input phase, concentrated at t=1-4 (never at t=0); rate falls off sharply after t=5, with a small, weak tail in the delimiter/copy phases. Within early positions it fires when the current or recent inputs come from a preferred token set: current input m,t,o,p,i (also e,x,g), previous or two-back input m,t,p,i,1,2,z. Strongest activations come from runs of these tokens, e.g. m m t or t m t at t=1-2 (top examples). Requiring at least 2 of current/prev/prev2 to be in the set raises precision to 0.63 but cuts recall to 0.33. It does not fire at t=0, rarely late in long inputs, and only weakly during copying. The behavior looks like a graded, distributed recency sum over token identities, so boolean predicates top out near F1 0.43 on dev.
